topic: How do phase perturbations in GEO satellite channels impact link budget calculations and required power margins for SINR constraints?
consensus_response: Phase perturbations in GEO satellite channels alter the array factor, introducing random fluctuations in the carrier phase that distort the radiation pattern. This leads to increased interference and reduced signal quality, resulting in a decreased Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR). The distortion of the array factor reduces Effective Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP), requiring an increase in transmit power or a decrease in interference tolerance. This compromises Average Used Power (AUP) and Average Used Bandwidth (AUB), affecting link budget calculations and required power margins.
reference_context: Phase perturbations, atmospheric impairments, and channel hardening were discussed in the reference context, with a focus on their impact on satellite communication systems.
